search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; reuse/fresh evidence composition; conditional e-processes; predictable post-freeze audit adaptation; finite-budget measurement validity

public_sources.title: Safe testing
public_sources.authors: Peter Grunwald; Rianne de Heide; Wouter Koolen
public_sources.used_scope: Proposition 2 states that running products of conditional e-variables are test supermartingales/e-processes, and the just-in-time discussion permits constructing the next conditional e-variable from all information available before the next fresh batch as long as conditional safety is retained. This is the external basis for multiplying a selection-corrected development e-value by a fresh-audit conditional e-process and for letting fresh betting strategy depend on frozen pre-audit state.

public_sources.title: The only admissible way of merging arbitrary e-values
public_sources.used_scope: Weighted arithmetic averages are the only admissible mergers for arbitrary e-values. Used only to distinguish arbitrary same-stage merging from the stronger two-stage conditional structure below; the product construction does not contradict the arbitrary-merger result because the fresh e-process is conditionally valid given the development stage.

public_sources.title: Rao-Blackwellized e-variables
public_sources.authors: Dante de Roos; Ben Chugg; Peter Grunwald; Aaditya Ramdas
public_sources.used_scope: Provides recent e-variable/e-process results centered on Jensen and concave utility. Used as supporting context for safe concave transforms; the exact e-to-e transform lemma below is a worker-local Jensen derivation.

public_sources.title: Sequential testing of conditionally constrained hypotheses
public_sources.used_scope: Characterizes e-processes for finitely conditionally constrained hypotheses and reports a complete-class result in which predictable products of affine one-step e-variables dominate. Used as support for prioritizing predictable fresh-stage betting rather than retrospective evidence reweighting; not claimed to cover the full adaptive-agent null without its stated conditional-constraint assumptions.

public_sources.title: Carefree multiple testing with e-processes
public_sources.authors: Yury Tavyrikov; Jelle J. Goeman; Rianne de Heide
public_sources.used_scope: Shows that naive multiple-testing operations on suprema of e-processes can lose advertised error control and develops adjuster-based FDR-sup control under arbitrary dependence. Added as a later frontier for repeated candidate streams; not used to change the single-candidate derivations here.

conditional_product_gate.setup: Let D be reused development data. Adaptive selection on D produces a frozen candidate and a selection-corrected global e-value S(D) with E_0[S]<=1 under the global null. On genuinely fresh audit data, let F_t be a conditional e-process for the frozen candidate with F_0=1 and E[F_t | D,A_{<t}]<=F_{t-1}.
conditional_product_gate.construction: For any nonnegative development-stage transform h with E[h(S)]<=1, define W_0=h(S) and W_t=h(S)F_t. Then E[W_0]<=1 and conditional on D the fresh stage is a nonnegative supermartingale, so the two-stage process is anytime-valid at the original alpha without branchwise alpha splitting.
conditional_product_gate.predictable_adaptation: The fresh factors/betting fractions used to build F_t may depend arbitrarily on S and all other frozen pre-audit information, and then on past fresh audit outcomes, provided each next factor remains conditionally e-valid before its outcome is observed. This is a safe way to exploit realized reuse evidence; it does not retrospectively increase the weight assigned to already-observed S.
conditional_product_gate.scope_guard: Fresh-audit conditional validity must hold for the selected frozen candidate. Reusing development observations in the fresh factor breaks this product argument unless separately corrected.

affine_start_product_dominates_fixed_con.definitions: For fixed a in [0,1], prior checkpoint used C_t=aS+(1-a)F_t. Define P_t=(1-a+aS)F_t. Both start at C_0=P_0=1-a+aS. P is valid by the conditional-product argument because h_a(S)=1-a+aS is itself an e-value.
affine_start_product_dominates_fixed_con.pathwise_relation: P_t-C_t=aS(F_t-1). If C_0 is below a rejection threshold c>1 and C_t later crosses c, necessarily F_t>1, hence P_t>=C_t at that time. Therefore P never rejects later than C for the same a,S,F path, while preserving the same t=0 evidence; strict improvement occurs whenever S>0 and a later crossing happens with F_t>1.
affine_start_product_dominates_fixed_con.consequence: In this two-stage fresh-audit structure, the fixed convex merger from the previous checkpoint is rejection-dominated by reinvesting the valid transformed development wealth into the conditionally valid fresh audit. This does not imply products are valid for arbitrary dependent e-values.

concave_e_to_e_transform_family.lemma: If h:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity) is concave and nondecreasing with h(1)<=1, then for every e-value S, E[h(S)]<=h(E[S])<=h(1)<=1 by Jensen. Thus h(S) is again an e-value.
concave_e_to_e_transform_family.use: A fixed/disjoint-meta-tuned transform can hedge how much selection-corrected reuse evidence becomes starting audit wealth. Power transforms boost S<1 relative to raw S but attenuate large S; affine transforms retain a floor when S is tiny. No single transform is uniformly best under alternatives.
concave_e_to_e_transform_family.scope_guard: Choosing the transform after inspecting the current S is not justified by this lemma unless the resulting composite h is itself proven e-preserving. Tune transform parameters only from protocol design/disjoint meta-data or prove a separate calibration theorem.

worker_local_simulation.purpose: Finite-budget stress test of the structural product-vs-convex claim; not a deployed-agent performance claim.
worker_local_simulation.fresh_sign_process: PACE-like fixed sign bet: candidate-only factor 1.5, incumbent-only factor 0.5, concordant factor 1.

null_sanity_check.S_distribution: S=5 with probability .1 and S=5/9 otherwise, so E[S]=1 exactly.
null_sanity_check.fresh_null: q=.5, fixed sign bet .75, budget 200, 120k trajectories per rho.
null_sanity_check.interpretation: All were below alpha=.05, consistent with the proof; simulation is only a sanity check and not the validity argument.

worker_local_simulation.hard_switch_note: The equal-risk hard-switch comparison used beta_r=beta_f=1-sqrt(.95)=.0253206, threshold 39.4936, when conditional S was below that threshold. It can save all fresh cost on sufficiently huge reuse evidence but is substantially less powerful for moderate S because it spends risk separately instead of pooling fresh evidence.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Convert selection-corrected reused-dev evidence into valid starting wealth h(S), then multiply by a conditionally valid fresh-audit e-process. Let fresh betting strategy depend predictably on frozen pre-audit state.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct tower-property/supermartingale derivation; Safe Testing Proposition 2 and just-in-time conditional e-variable principle; worker-local finite-budget stress test.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Requires valid global S and genuinely conditionally valid fresh audit for the frozen candidate.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Replace C_t=aS+(1-a)F_t by P_t=(1-a+aS)F_t for the same fixed a whenever fresh conditional composition assumptions hold.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Exact pathwise dominance at every later convex rejection plus global e-process proof; simulation showed material finite-budget gains.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Dominance is specific to the two-stage conditional structure. It is not a generic rule to multiply arbitrary e-values computed on overlapping/dependent data.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Use a protocol-fixed/disjoint-meta-tuned concave nondecreasing e-to-e transform h(S), such as affine or power transforms, before fresh-audit reinvestment to trade robustness to tiny S against leverage from large S.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Jensen derivation and recent e-variable concave-utility literature.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Current-S-dependent transform selection is not free; the full selected transform must itself preserve e-validity.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected in the conditional-fresh setting: 'fixed convex averaging is the natural final reuse/fresh merger.' It is valid but pathwise rejection-dominated by safe reinvestment when the fresh stage is conditionally valid.

Narrowed: 'realized reuse evidence cannot influence fresh testing because that is data-dependent weighting.' It cannot be retrospectively reweighted for free, but it may safely determine the next fresh conditional bet before the next fresh outcome.

Rejected: 'multiplication of any two e-values is valid.' Multiplication here relies on sequential/conditional validity and separate fresh data; overlapping arbitrary e-values generally require another merger such as averaging.

Narrowed: 'hard switch is needed to avoid double spending alpha.' A single conditional-product process can pool development and fresh evidence under one alpha; hard switching remains relevant mainly as a cost/availability policy rather than a validity necessity.
